zuutf

Every Unicode encoding R meets, validated and converted at memory speed, with the exact position of the first error.

zuutf validates text and converts it between UTF-8, UTF-16 (LE and BE), UTF-32 (LE and BE) and Latin-1, counts characters, detects encodings, and encodes and decodes Base64. It does this with a bundled copy of simdutf, which picks SIMD code for the processor at first use. Other packages can call the same functions from C through a registered table (vignette("linking")).

Installation 

install.packages("zuutf")

The development version is on GitHub:

# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("pedrobtz/zuutf")

Validation, with the position of the first error 

library(zuutf)

utf_valid(c("plain", "café", NA))
#> [1]  TRUE  TRUE    NA

bad <- as.raw(c(0x61, 0x62, 0xe2, 0x82, 0x63))   # a truncated euro sign
utf_valid(bad)
#> [1] FALSE
utf_error_at(bad)
#> [1] 3

UTF-16 from Windows tools 

bytes <- readBin("export.csv", "raw", file.size("export.csv"))
utf_detect(bytes)                 # the byte-order mark decides
#> [1] "UTF-16LE"
text <- utf_decode(bytes)         # from = "auto"; the BOM is dropped

Ill-formed input raises a classed error by default; invalid = "replace" writes U+FFFD as web browsers do, and invalid = "na" gives NA:

utf_decode(as.raw(c(0x61, 0xff, 0x62)), "UTF-8", invalid = "replace")
#> [1] "a�b"

Base64 

s <- base64_encode(charToRaw("hello, world"))
s
#> [1] "aGVsbG8sIHdvcmxk"
rawToChar(base64_decode(s))
#> [1] "hello, world"
base64_encode(as.raw(0:63), url = TRUE, pad = FALSE)

Decoding is forgiving by default, as browsers’ is; forgiving = FALSE reads RFC 4648 strictly.
